text: The biggest shark that ever lived. So what killed it?
Megalodon. Around fifteen meters long, maybe more.
For years, scientists thought it vanished about two point six million years ago.
Then, in 2019, a team rechecked the fossil record of California and Mexico.
The real fossils stop around three point six million years ago. A million years earlier.
Suspect one: a cooling ocean, breaking its range apart.
Suspect two: food. Its prey was changing.
Suspect three: a smaller, faster rival. The great white shark.
Great whites appeared about four million years ago. Soon after, megalodon was gone.
The researchers suggest the newcomer may have outcompeted the giant.
Verdict: unsolved. The suspects are on the board, but no one has closed the case.
Who do you think did it?
